payload.chart:
The transport is ruled, so this chart covers only the choices the ruling leaves open. Pruned cells carry their reason.

ROW 1 - where the brief's key lives. (a) URL fragment, never transmitted by the browser - chosen, and the design's own stated shape; PROBED working. (b) query parameter - pruned: it reaches the host in every request and in its logs, which defeats the point. (c) a second ntfy message - pruned: two messages to correlate, both retained by the relay, no gain.

ROW 2 - what the store holds. (a) ciphertext plus an inline decryptor in one self-contained page - chosen; PROBED: the marker is absent from the stored body and it still serves as text/html. (b) plaintext HTML - pruned: fails C3 outright. (c) ciphertext with a separate decryptor script - pruned: a second fetch, a second thing to host, and the CSP surface grows for nothing.

ROW 3 - when the notification goes out. (a) after confirming the page serves - chosen; the measured window is ~1s, so the cost is small and the failure mode (tapping into a 404) is removed. (b) immediately, optimistically - pruned: it is the exact failure the design recorded from its own dry run. (c) on a delay guessed from the documented ~60s - pruned: measurement beats folklore, and a fixed sleep is both slower and less certain than a check.

ROW 4 - what happens when the brief cannot be published. (a) send the card anyway with two actions, and record the failure - chosen; it is the ladder degrading as designed. (b) abort the announcement - pruned: a host outage would become a gate outage, failing the veto criterion. (c) send the card and stay silent about the failure - pruned: that is precisely today's defect, one level up.

ROW 5 - how the answer URL is built. (a) absolutize the bare topic against the configured base at send time - chosen, and exactly what v1 does; its own comment names the trap. (b) store absolute URLs in the pairing config - pruned: the base would then be duplicated in two places and could disagree. (c) a scheme-like token such as answer:<topic> - pruned, and it is worth recording that this WAS the shipped behaviour: it is not a URL, the phone refuses it, and the owner found it by tapping.

ROW 6 - who decides that a human will adjudicate. (a) the caller announcing the gate states it - chosen: the loop already knows whether it is running delegated. (b) infer from configuration - pruned: configuration says whether a phone exists, not who decides. (c) always publish - pruned: the owner explicitly does not want traffic during self-blessing runs.
payload.shortlist: One combination seeded: 1a + 2a + 3a + 4a + 5a + 6a. Every alternative above was eliminated on a stated failure rather than a preference - three of them (2b, 4b, 4c, 5c) breach a veto criterion or reproduce the current defect, and the rest lose on measurement or duplication. Elaborating a second candidate would mean elaborating one already known to fail, which the design names as decision theater. Static partitioning for the seeded combination is the clustering already recorded: cluster A gates the work, cluster B is the optional brief pipeline, cluster C is the summons that must fire regardless, cluster D receives the answer, with reporting and credential-withholding as constraints over all of it. Feasibility is not rough - every mechanic in the chosen column was exercised live at run-bfd564ff9add.
